prompt: Break down our new onboarding flow plan into implementation-ready features and put it in the plans folder. The idea: right now when someone signs up they just land on an empty dashboard and have no idea what to do. We want a guided onboarding flow that gets them to their first meaningful action faster. Should probably have a few steps and some kind of progress indicator. We haven't picked exact steps yet, just know it needs to feel quick and not annoying. No backend/tech stack details yet, just want the plan turned into features.

assertions.text: The run either asks clarifying questions about the missing specifics (onboarding steps, tech stack, definition of 'first meaningful action') or explicitly labels its choices as assumptions/a draft rather than presenting invented specifics as settled requirements
If clarifying questions are asked, they target the actual gaps in the prompt (what the onboarding steps are, what platform/stack, what counts as done) rather than generic filler questions
The run does not silently fabricate a fully detailed, confident implementation plan (specific tech choices, specific onboarding step content) with no acknowledgment that these were invented
If plans/ files are written at all, they are clearly framed as a starting draft for discussion, not a final spec
